title: Grandmaster Challenge: Plastic in the Barangay

passage.title: The Plastic Problem in Barangay San Roque
passage.text:
Every rainy season, the creek in Barangay San Roque overflows, and every year the reason is the same: plastic. Sachets, bags, and bottles clog the drainage canals until the water has nowhere to go but the streets.

In 2023, the barangay council tried something new. Instead of simply fining people who littered, they set up a "plastic bank." Residents could bring clean, sorted plastic to a collection point every Saturday and receive points. The points could be exchanged for rice, cooking oil, or school supplies. A local recycling company bought the plastic from the barangay, which paid for the goods.

The results surprised even the council. In the first six months, residents brought in more than four tons of plastic. Children became the most eager collectors; some organized teams and competed to fill the most sacks. The canals, cleaned by volunteers at the same time, stayed clear through the next rainy season, and for the first time in a decade the creek did not flood the main road.

Critics point out that the plastic bank does not stop plastic from being made or sold. Sachets are still the cheapest way for poor families to buy shampoo and coffee. "We are cleaning up a problem that someone else keeps creating," one councilor admitted. Still, most residents say the program changed how they see waste. As one grandmother put it, "Before, plastic was garbage. Now it is rice."

words.meaning: to block something so that nothing can pass through
words.example: Hair can clog the shower drain.

words.meaning: very keen and excited to do something
words.example: The eager students raised their hands.

words.meaning: people who point out problems or disagree with something
words.example: Critics of the plan said it would cost too much.

items.prompt: Why does the creek overflow every rainy season?
choices: Too much rain falls.
Plastic clogs the drainage canals.
The creek is too small.
Volunteers block the road.
items.why: "Sachets, bags, and bottles clog the drainage canals until the water has nowhere to go but the streets."

items.prompt: "They set up a plastic bank." What does bank mean here?
choices: The side of a river
A place where something is collected and stored for exchange
To lean to one side
A row of lights
items.why: Residents deposit plastic and get points, like a bank that stores and exchanges things.

items.prompt: "Residents could bring clean, sorted plastic to a collection point every Saturday." What does point mean here?
choices: A score in a game
The sharp end of a pencil
A particular place
The main idea of a speech
items.why: The sentence says residents bring plastic there, so point is a place. In the next sentence, points means scores to exchange.

items.prompt: How was the barangay able to pay for the rice, oil, and school supplies?
choices: Residents paid a fee to join.
The mayor donated the money.
Fines from littering covered the cost.
A recycling company bought the plastic from the barangay.
items.why: "A local recycling company bought the plastic from the barangay, which paid for the goods."

choices: The council fined people who littered.
Residents could get rice, cooking oil, or school supplies.
In 2023 the council started a plastic bank where residents traded sorted plastic for points they could exchange for goods, paid for by a recycling company.
Collection happened every Saturday.
items.why: Choice C keeps the whole plan in order. Choice A is what the council stopped doing, and choices B and D are single details.

items.prompt: Why did the creek NOT flood the main road the next rainy season?
choices: The canals stayed clear after plastic was collected and volunteers cleaned them.
The rains were lighter that year.
The council built a wider creek.
Sachets were banned in the barangay.
items.why: "The canals, cleaned by volunteers at the same time, stayed clear through the next rainy season, and... the creek did not flood the main road."

items.prompt: "The canals... stayed clear through the next rainy season." What does clear mean here?
choices: Easy to understand
Free of anything blocking the way
See-through like glass
Without clouds
items.why: The canals used to be clogged with plastic; clear means nothing was blocking them anymore.

items.prompt: Which detail does NOT belong in a summary of this passage?
choices: Plastic clogs the canals and floods the creek every rainy season.
The barangay set up a plastic bank that traded plastic for goods.
Some children organized teams and competed to fill the most sacks.
Critics say the program does not stop plastic from being sold.
items.why: The children's teams are an example, not a main point. The other choices are the problem, the program, and the criticism.

items.prompt: What is the author's main purpose?
choices: To entertain with a story about a grandmother
To inform readers about a barangay program and its results
To persuade readers to buy sachets
To describe a creek
items.why: The text reports what the council did, gives numbers, and presents both results and criticism.

items.prompt: Why did the author include the paragraph about the critics?
choices: To prove the plastic bank failed
To persuade readers to stop buying sachets
To entertain readers with a councilor's joke
To show the program's limits as well as its success
items.why: The paragraph admits the bank "does not stop plastic from being made or sold" but still reports that most residents see waste differently.

items.prompt: Why did the author end with the grandmother's words, "Before, plastic was garbage. Now it is rice"?
choices: To show in one line how residents' view of waste changed
To explain how rice is grown
To warn that plastic is dangerous to eat
To describe the grandmother's house
items.why: The sentence before says the program "changed how they see waste." Her words give that change in a single picture.

choices: Children competed to fill sacks of plastic.
A barangay fought flooding by paying residents in goods for plastic; the canals stayed clear and the road did not flood, though critics say it does not stop plastic from being sold.
Sachets are the cheapest way to buy shampoo.
A grandmother said plastic is now rice.
items.why: It covers the problem, the program, the result, and the criticism in order.
